title: Cartesian pushout-product axiom for categorical equivalences
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, degreewise products and pushouts in a fixed universe, and categorical equivalences and the Joyal model structure of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. For degreewise injective simplicial maps $a:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $b:C\hookrightarrow D$, the cartesian pushout-product
$$a\mathbin\square b:(B\times C)\amalg_{A\times C}(A\times D)\longrightarrow B\times D$$
is degreewise injective. If either $a$ or $b$ is a categorical equivalence, then $a\mathbin\square b$ is a categorical equivalence. These assertions concern the unmarked Joyal model structure, not only inner-anodyne maps, and all constructions stay in the input universe.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.4 (printed p.92, PDF p.110): products preserve categorical equivalences, together with the trivial-cofibration weak factorization system of Theorem 2.2.5.1. The Cartesian axiom follows by pushing out a×C and applying two-out-of-three to a×D. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED archive. No Stacks tag states the unmarked Joyal-model assertion.
